<solution_file path="src/t02_load_eurostat.py">
import pandas as pd
import csv
import io
import os


def main():
    # Read selected indicators
    selected_indicators_path = "outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv"
    selected_indicators = pd.read_csv(selected_indicators_path)

    # Create a set of selected indicator_ids for efficient lookup
    selected_indicator_ids = set(selected_indicators["indicator_id"].unique())

    # Read the Eurostat city values
    city_values_path = "inputs/eurostat/eurostat_city_values_sample.csv"
    city_values = pd.read_csv(city_values_path)

    # Filter to only include selected indicators
    filtered = city_values[city_values["indicator_id"].isin(selected_indicator_ids)].copy()

    # Remove duplicates based on city_id, year, indicator_id
    # Keep first occurrence
    filtered = filtered.drop_duplicates(subset=["city_id", "year", "indicator_id"], keep="first")

    # Select only the required columns in the correct order
    output_columns = ["city_id", "city_name", "year", "indicator_id", "indicator_name", "value", "unit"]
    filtered = filtered[output_columns]

    # Write to CSV with RFC 4180 compliance
    output_path = "outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv"
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_path), exist_ok=True)

    with open(output_path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f, quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL, lineterminator="\r\n")

        # Write header
        writer.writerow(output_columns)

        # Write data rows
        for _, row in filtered.iterrows():
            writer.writerow([row[col] for col in output_columns])

    print(f"Wrote {len(filtered)} rows to {output_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
</solution_file>
